title: We used AI-assisted art and code to build Bounce Clash, a slingshot RPG for Android
author: hoangbach1502
selftext:
I’m one of the developers at Golden Tier Studio. Bounce Clash combines pinball-style aiming with RPG team building: launch a hero, bounce off walls, and hit teammates to trigger combos. It is available on Google Play.



We used generative AI for character art and development assistance. One practical lesson was that generating a pose sheet did not give us a usable animation atlas automatically. We still had to measure the regions, register the bodies across poses, import the assets, and inspect them in the actual Unity battle screen. A technically valid atlas could still look wrong in motion.



For us, the useful split has been AI for generating candidates and assisting implementation, followed by checks against the actual game: footage, imported assets, save isolation, and gameplay behavior. The combat shown is real Unity gameplay, not generated video.



Gameplay: [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PtTv4a5V\_3o](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PtTv4a5V_3o)

Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.goldentier.PinballArena](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.goldentier.PinballArena)



I’m sharing this as the developer of a commercial game. If you try it, I’d be interested in whether aiming and hero-to-hero combos make sense in the first few minutes. For other AI-assisted developers: how are you checking visual consistency once generated assets are actually moving in-game?
